text:
Anna (Support): Hey team — incoming from AcmeCorp. They say their monthly credits dropped to 0 on the 12th even though their billing date is the 1st. Customer attached logs showing 429s and an `x-reset` header that points to a time earlier than their timezone start. Quote from ticket: "We were live on the 11th and suddenly started getting quota errors. It looks like the meter flipped overnight and we lost a whole day of credits."

Customer - AcmeCorp: More details — we were on Standard plan, used ~1.1M tokens in the billing month. At ~2026-02-12 03:42 UTC our service started returning 429 with body: `Quota exhausted`. Our dashboard still showed remaining credits until ~2026-02-12 00:05 PST.

Tom (Billing): Thanks Anna. Quick sanity check — can you confirm the customer’s billing cycle is anchored to the 1st? Also ask if they changed subscription tier mid-cycle. Proration or plan changes can alter visible credit windows. :thinking:

Anna (Support): I asked for account id and if they had an upgrade/downgrade. Customer says they upgraded from Developer -> Standard on 2026-02-11 23:50 PST and paid via card. They say the dashboard showed rollover credits then disappeared.

Jia (Engineering): Hmm, upgrading mid-cycle can trigger immediate recalculation: we apply remaining credit as a prorated amount and new allocation starts at next reset boundary. But that shouldn’t remove already-consumed tokens retroactively. Can they share the exact request IDs around the first 429 so we can check server-side records?

Customer - AcmeCorp: Provided two request ids: req_9a3f and req_9a41. I pasted the curl that hits the API and shows headers:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-quota-remaining: 0
x-quota-reset: 1676217600
x-request-id: req_9a3f
content-type: application/json
\n{"error":{"message":"Quota exhausted"}}
```

Tom (Billing): x-quota-reset of `1676217600` corresponds to 2023-02-12 00:00:00 UTC — that timestamp looks like a month boundary but off by year. Could be a clock skew or stale header from cache. Ask them for both the dashboard billing start/end timestamps (the UI shows human-friendly times).

Anna (Support): Customer attached a screenshot: dashboard billing period = Feb 1 — Feb 28 (PST). They insist their usage was below the limit before the 12th. Also noted an automatic promo credit applied on Feb 10 which reduced billable allocation.

Jia (Engineering): Two hypotheses: 1) promo credit applied and our allocation calc rebalanced available tokens immediately, effectively subtracting the promo-adjusted quota from their remaining tokens — this can make remaining tokens drop if we re-evaluate the full-month allowance; 2) cache or legacy CDN returned a stale `x-quota-reset` header from a previous account state. I’ll pull the logs for `req_9a3f` and `req_9a41` and check the billing-adjustment event stream for Feb 10–12.

RedwoodBot: billing-event: account_update promo_applied account=acct_42 time=2026-02-10T08:12:05Z (auto-prorate=true)

Jia (Engineering): Found the request traces — both requests routed through edge node `edge-7` which had a cached quota object from 02/10 after the promo application. The cache TTL was larger than expected and edge returned `x-quota-reset` tied to the older object. However, server-side consumption counters were accurate and show the customer did exceed the adjusted monthly allocation by ~120k tokens on the 12th. So the 429s are valid relative to the post-promo allocation.

Tom (Billing): Ok — so the user saw the UI show an earlier number because the UI was reading from the pre-promo materialized view for a few minutes before the backfill. That discrepancy window is unfortunate. We should explain: when a promo or plan change kills some of the month’s remaining allocation, it can look like credits disappeared. We need to confirm whether we displayed a warning at promo time.

Anna (Support): Customer says they weren’t shown a warning and want a partial credit because they weren’t aware the promo reduced their remaining tokens immediately. They claim the UI said "Your credits updated; see billing" but no clear callout.

Jia (Engineering): For remediation: 1) Offer to run a replay of their requests during 2026-02-11 20:00–2026-02-12 06:00 to confirm which ones were accepted vs rejected. 2) Provide the exact event ids and timestamps showing the promo application and reallocation. 3) We should add an internal follow-up to reduce edge cache TTL for quota objects to <60s to avoid stale headers.

Tom (Billing): From billing side, suggest offering one-time courtesy credit covering the 120k tokens and add a line-item explaining the adjustment and reason. Flagging for legal if promo terms say otherwise.

Anna (Support): I’ll propose the one-time credit and share the event timeline. Customer requested a clear explanation in plain language about why credits can "disappear" mid-month. Drafting this: 

Anna (Support): Plain language explanation (to send to customer): "When we apply promotions or change your plan mid-cycle, we recalculate how many tokens you get for the rest of the billing period. Sometimes this recalculation reduces the number of remaining tokens — that’s what happened here after the promo. Our edge cache briefly showed the older numbers, which made the dashboard look inconsistent. The 429s reflect the new, lower allocation. We can issue a one-time credit while we fix cache TTLs."

Customer - AcmeCorp: Thanks. Accepts the credit offer but asks we also improve the notice in the UI. :thumbsup:

Tom (Billing): Thanks everyone. Action items: Anna — send credit + timeline, Jia — schedule cache TTL fix and provide logs, Billing — finalize credit amount and add explanation to invoice. I’ll create a follow-up ticket for UI wording. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
